Based on our review, there is evidence that parts of the timer‐driver code (especially in snd_timer_user_ioctl and the related start/stop/release functions) rely on only partially localized locking. In one IOCTL branch (the TREAD command) a mutex (tread_sem) is used to protect access to some fields of the private snd_timer_user structure, but the other IOCTL commands (such as START, STOP, CONTINUE, PAUSE) and even the release function do not take a lock that covers access to the shared state (for example, the timeri pointer and other fields). That is exactly the kind of race‐condition (TOCTOU) situation described by CWE‑362.
